questions.q:
Give the approximate dates of:
(a) the Baroque period
(b) the Classical period

(a) Name two ornaments common in Baroque music. [1]
(b) Which keyboard instrument replaced the harpsichord in the Classical period? [1]
ms: (a) any two of: trill, mordent, turn, appoggiatura (both needed)
(b) piano / fortepiano
questions.model: (a) trill and mordent (b) the fortepiano (early piano)

questions.q:
An extract is described like this: "A small string orchestra is accompanied by a harpsichord. A group of two violins and a cello alternates with the full string section. The dynamics switch suddenly between loud and soft, and a short theme is passed from part to part."
(a) Name the period. [1]
(b) Name the genre. [1]
(c) Give two features from the description that support your answers. [2]
ms: (a) Baroque
(b) concerto grosso
(c) harpsichord continuo
(c) concertino (2 violins + cello) contrasted with the ripieno
(c) terraced dynamics
(c) imitation / imitative texture
(c) any two, 1 each
questions.model: (a) Baroque. (b) Concerto grosso. (c) A small concertino of two violins and cello contrasts with the ripieno, and the dynamics are terraced.

questions.q: Give four features of a Classical minuet and trio.
ms: triple time (3/4)
ternary structure overall: minuet – trio – minuet (da capo)
each section is in binary form with repeats
trio contrasts with the minuet (e.g. lighter/thinner texture, different instrumentation, sometimes a different key)
balanced phrases (e.g. 4 + 4 bars) / clear perfect and imperfect cadences
moderate, elegant dance tempo
homophonic texture
questions.model: It is in 3/4 at a moderate dance tempo. The overall form is minuet – trio – minuet (ternary), with each part in binary form with repeats. The trio contrasts with a thinner texture. Phrases are balanced in four-bar units ending with clear cadences.

questions.q: Compare typical Baroque and Classical music in terms of texture, the bass part, melody and dynamics.
ms: Texture: Baroque often polyphonic/imitative; Classical mainly homophonic
Bass: Baroque has basso continuo (harpsichord/organ + cello/bass)
Bass: Classical has no continuo; accompaniment such as Alberti bass
Melody: Baroque long, ornamented lines spun out, with sequences
Melody: Classical balanced, symmetrical phrases (question and answer)
Dynamics: Baroque terraced
Dynamics: Classical gradual crescendo/diminuendo and sforzandi
max 3 if only one period is described
questions.model: Baroque textures are often polyphonic and imitative, whereas Classical music is mostly homophonic. A Baroque bass line is played by a continuo of harpsichord and cello, while Classical composers use accompaniment patterns like the Alberti bass. Baroque melodies are long and ornamented, spun out with sequences; Classical melodies fall into balanced four-bar phrases. Baroque dynamics are terraced, but Classical music uses crescendos and diminuendos.
questions.tip: For 'compare', link each Baroque point to the Classical point on the same element.

questions.q: Explain how the concerto changed between the Baroque period and the Classical period.
ms: Baroque: concerto grosso (concertino vs ripieno) as well as solo concerto
Baroque: fast movements usually in ritornello form
Baroque: basso continuo with harpsichord / string-based orchestra
Classical: solo concerto becomes the main type (often piano, also violin, clarinet, horn)
Classical: first movements use sonata form (often with an orchestral and a solo exposition)
Classical: a cadenza for the soloist near the end of the movement
Classical: larger orchestra with woodwind, horns, (trumpets, timpani); continuo disappears
Classical: gradual dynamics; contrast of two themes
questions.model: In the Baroque, concertos were either concerti grossi (concertino against ripieno) or solo concertos, with fast movements in ritornello form over a harpsichord continuo and a mostly string orchestra. In the Classical period the solo concerto, often for piano, became the main type. First movements used sonata form and included a cadenza for the soloist. The orchestra grew to include woodwind and horns, and the continuo disappeared.
